Based on the available source material, the solution context is supported by implementation and user documentation that provides overviews, illustrations, procedures, and examples for planning-related capabilities, including guidance on user interaction, modeling exercises, strategy configuration, and implementation activities. These materials indicate a documented foundation for how planning components are used, how strategies and constraints can be understood through guided exercises, and how implementation specialists and systems integrators configure the environment.

For Archlin, the current-state challenge is defined as poor inventory planning. Within the available source documents, the relevant solution perspective is one in which planning functionality is supported by user guides, implementation guides, strategy and parameter references, and associated help content accessible through the user interface. The documentation set also includes release information for new or updated functionality, installation guidance, user guidance for the web user interface, and descriptions of functions used with strategy files and global parameters used to control planner behavior. This establishes a structured reference base for implementation and ongoing use, although Archlin-specific process details, organizational roles, and baseline metrics are .

The implementation approach for Archlin’s Phase 1 Demand Planning initiative should therefore be understood as being grounded in documented procedures, examples, and configuration guidance. The source material shows that implementation content is intended to support optimization and scheduling components, environment configuration, and integration setup with external systems through supporting reference documentation such as the data dictionary and infrastructure services API guidance. Where Archlin-specific integration design, planning model scope, master data requirements, or deployment sequencing are concerned, the details are TBD based on the source documents provided.

The expected business intent of Archlin’s investment is to improve planning effectiveness in response to the identified inventory planning issue, while leveraging a documented application framework that includes user help, implementation guidance, modeling exercises, and parameter-based control of planning behavior. While the provided materials do not state Archlin-specific target outcomes, quantified benefits, or success measures, they do support an implementation model in which users, implementation specialists, and systems integrators can work from established documentation to configure, operate, and sustain the planning solution in a controlled manner.

Archlin is undertaking this initiative to address poor inventory planning through a Phase 1 focus on Demand Planning in its SAP S/$HANA environment. Based on the available source material, the implementation approach is supported by Transportation Planner documentation that describes a configurable planning environment with optimization, shipment scheduling, user interface, and server-based processing capabilities. While the uploaded source documents do not provide Archlin-specific current-state process maps, organizational details, or system landscape architecture beyond SAP S/$HANA and the stated pain point, they do establish the configurable technical framework that can support a structured planning implementation for Archlin.

The available documentation indicates that Transportation Planner includes core components such as the Shipment Scheduling Engine, Shipment Scheduler user interface, Optimizer Server, Routing and Rating server, Transportation Planner user interface, Parameter File Editor, and Strategy File Editor. The documented process model also shows that optimization works within a hierarchy that includes a plan, defined as a set of trips and loads generated by the Optimizer using shipment, location, carrier rate, and hub information, and a web, defined as a set of dependent trips and loads that cannot be broken down further due to shipment and load dependencies. For Archlin, these documented capabilities provide the underlying solution context for configuring and executing planning logic, even though Archlin-specific planning parameters, master data structures, and business rules are .

<IMAGE id="08b333823261"/>

From an implementation perspective, the source documents show that most Transportation Planner configuration details are stored in the tpConfig.xml file, which contains Basic product settings, CIS, database information, engines, Shipment Consolidation Engine, Shipment Scheduler Engine, TM request handler, web applications, Shipment Consolidation UI, Shipment Scheduler Viewer UI, installer settings, and Transportation Planner instance groups. The documentation further states that many configuration parameters contain Basic and Advanced sections, with Basic parameters intended for average users and Advanced parameters for experienced users. It also specifies that each time changes are made to the configuration file, the configureTP.py script must be executed to reconfigure the Transportation Planner environment. For Archlin, this points to a controlled configuration and deployment model in which planning behavior, server interactions, and user access are governed through explicit configuration artifacts rather than ad hoc setup.

The implementation guide also identifies setup.xml as the configuration file used by the Shipment Scheduler Engine and notes that user interface access is available for configuration information. Additional documented setup structures include instance-specific setup files such as Setup-OPT.xml and Setup-RR.xml when default installation values are used for instance creation, with explicit guidance that the appropriate setup-.xml file must be edited for the relevant implementation. For Archlin, this indicates that implementation will require disciplined instance-level configuration and environment management aligned to the selected deployment model. However, the specific instances, environments, and naming conventions to be used for Archlin are .

The source material also describes multiple run-time modes for the planning environment. Transportation Planner servers can be run by executing the appropriate python script from the Transportation Planner Launcher, by configuring servers to start at system startup, by starting servers from the Transportation Planner User Interface, or by starting servers from the Infrastructure Services CIS Manager. In addition, the documentation states that Transportation Planner can run the Shipment Consolidation Engine in server mode to handle requests from Transportation Manager through TMRS without user interaction, can run in interactive mode through the user interface, can run the Shipment Scheduler Engine with direct optimization requests, and can run the Shipment Scheduler user interface to select an input plan, solve the plan, and view results in tables and charts. For Archlin, these documented operating modes support a flexible implementation approach that can accommodate both controlled server-based execution and interactive planning activities as needed during solution deployment and adoption.

The strategy framework described in the source documentation is also relevant to Archlin’s implementation. The Optimizer uses a configurable text-based strategy file in which each line specifies an available function and arguments that control optimizer behavior. The sequence of functions and associated parameters can affect both performance and final load-build results, and the documentation states that strategy files can be customized during implementation. This establishes that Archlin’s solution can be tuned through configurable optimization logic, with implementation work expected to define and refine strategy behavior to support desired planning outcomes. Within the limits of the available source material, the expected result for Archlin is a configured planning environment capable of supporting optimized planning execution, controlled configuration management, and operational visibility through available user interfaces. sections.3.3:
Archlin’s Phase 1 scope focuses on enabling Supply Management capabilities in Kinaxis to address poor inventory planning, limited supply visibility, raw material shortage risks, and the inefficiencies caused by siloed Excel-based planning processes.

Archlin currently operates on SAP S/4HANA and uses partially automated, Excel-based planning processes that require significant manual consolidation and delay planning cycles.

Archlin business users emphasized the need for collaborative forecasting and improved visibility across regions to support more effective supply and inventory decisions.

Archlin supply planners highlighted recurring raw material shortages and requested exception-based alerts to improve responsiveness to supply constraints.

Archlin leadership expects measurable improvements in inventory reduction, planning cycle time, planner productivity, and the establishment of a single source of planning data within six months of go-live.

3.3.1 In-Scope Supply Management Capabilities

Archlin will generate constrained supply plans to support feasible supply decisions based on available supply, demand requirements, and operational constraints.

Archlin will identify material shortages to improve visibility into potential supply risks before they impact production or customer commitments.

Archlin will support capacity planning to evaluate whether production capacity is sufficient to meet planned supply requirements.

Archlin will use exception-based alerts so planners can focus on supply issues requiring action instead of manually reviewing all planning data.

Archlin will enable scenario analysis to compare supply alternatives and evaluate the impact of changing assumptions before finalizing plans.

Archlin will define safety stock policies to improve inventory planning and reduce the risk of stockouts.

Archlin will calculate inventory targets to support more disciplined inventory positioning across locations.

Archlin will monitor excess inventory to support inventory reduction and working-capital improvement objectives.

Archlin will track inventory turns to measure inventory performance and identify improvement opportunities.

Archlin will optimize stock across locations to improve supply availability and reduce unnecessary inventory buildup.

3.3.2 Required Interfaces for Phase 1

Archlin’s Phase 1 Kinaxis-enabled Supply Management process will require integration with SAP S/4HANA and related planning data sources for the following data objects.

Archlin Product Master data will be required to support item-level planning and supply analysis.

Archlin Customer Master data will be required to support customer-related demand and supply visibility.

Archlin Sales Orders will be required to reflect current demand signals in supply planning.

Archlin Inventory Balances will be required to provide visibility into available stock and inventory positions.

Archlin Purchase Orders will be required to provide visibility into expected inbound supply.

Archlin Production Orders will be required to provide visibility into planned and released production supply.

Archlin’s required data refresh frequency for the Phase 1 planning interfaces is every 4 hours.

3.3.3 Phase 1 Success Measures

Archlin will target inventory reduction greater than 15% through improved supply visibility, inventory planning, and exception-based management.

Archlin will target planning cycle reduction greater than 30% by reducing manual Excel consolidation and enabling more automated planning workflows.

Archlin will improve planner productivity by giving planners a centralized planning environment, actionable alerts, and better visibility to supply constraints.

Archlin will establish a single source of planning data to reduce silos and improve alignment across planning stakeholders.

Archlin will use forecast accuracy greater than 85% as a related planning success criterion where forecast inputs influence supply and inventory plans.

3.3.4 Key Design Considerations

Archlin’s Phase 1 design must reduce dependency on siloed Excel-based planning and support more automated planning execution.

Archlin’s Phase 1 design must provide planners with visibility into inventory balances, purchase orders, production orders, and material shortages.

Archlin’s Phase 1 design must support planner review of exceptions so supply risks can be prioritized and resolved efficiently.

Archlin’s Phase 1 design must support collaboration between planning stakeholders by using shared planning data and dashboard-based reporting.

Archlin’s Phase 1 design must maintain alignment with SAP S/4HANA as the ERP system of record for relevant master and transactional data.
